compiled.definition: Deletion Resolution Asymmetric Tautology: a proof-log format SAT solvers emit when they report unsatisfiable, so an independent checker can verify the claim.

reviews.intendedDefinition: A proof-log format for certifying that a CNF formula is unsatisfiable. Checking is polynomial in the combined formula and proof size; a proof need not have polynomial length in the original formula. A solver timeout is not such a certificate.
reviews.rationale: The earlier owner defines exactly the same UNSAT proof-log format and independent verification role. It makes no polynomial-original-formula certificate-length claim and no proof-only checking-time claim, so it is compatible with the combined-input-size qualification in the intended definition. Official DRAT-trim documentation checks additions against the current formula and proof.

compiled.definition: An oracle is a hypothetical black box answering membership questions for one fixed language, such as the halting problem. An oracle machine is a Turing machine allowed to consult it: after writing a query, it receives the yes/no answer in one computational step, while the work of writing the query still counts. This model compares computational power under an assumed extra capability; it does not supply a physical implementation of that capability.

reviews.intendedDefinition: An abstract subroutine that answers membership in one fixed language in one query step, after the machine has written the query. Writing a long query still costs time. Giving different machine classes the same oracle helps study proof techniques and relative computational power.
reviews.rationale: The refined earlier-owner wording and intended wording both use one fixed membership language, one-step answer after query writing, and charged query-writing work. Arora–Barak Definition3.6 explicitly defines the query tape/answer step. Its extra distinction between an oracle and its calling machine is compatible. This exact source definition is independently accepted; generated output must still be checked by root.

compiled.subject: theory
compiled.definition: PSPACE is the class of decision problems solvable with memory bounded by a polynomial in the input length. A PSPACE-complete decision problem is in that class and every problem in PSPACE reduces to it in polynomial time; no polynomial-time algorithm is known. Deciding whether a given DFA has an equivalent NFA within a supplied state bound is PSPACE-complete.

reviews.intendedDefinition: PSPACE-hard means every PSPACE problem reduces to the target by a polynomial-time many-one reduction. PSPACE-complete additionally requires membership in PSPACE; TQBF and ordinary regular-expression equivalence are examples.
reviews.rationale: Both definitions require membership in PSPACE and polynomial-time reduction of every PSPACE decision problem; the earlier owner uses a different valid example. Arora–Barak chapter4 establishes the class/completeness distinction and TQBF. The primary SIAM Jiang–Ravikumar1993 abstract explicitly proves the DFA-to-minimum-equivalent-NFA decision problem PSPACE-complete (primary search record retrieved; direct page open returned403). Acceptance is for PSPACE-complete/completeness only, not routing the bare PSPACE class to this heading.
